figures.title: This paper in the 13 components, against the field
figures.subtitle: Each box: what this paper does, then common practice across all sensors and how many ledger papers share it.

M01.field: Train voiced, use silent; modes reported apart
M01.note: Inherited Gaddy-corpus setup (voiced plus silent EMG in training); standard.

M02.note: Voiced-audio mels and phoneme alignment as teacher are the standard supervision for this corpus.

M03.note: Full-to-subset initialization helps at 4-6 electrodes but is unrepeated against a weak baseline, and channel dropout is neither new nor supported by Fig. 3 (p=0 best at 6 and 4).

M04.field: Silent and voiced results reported apart
M04.note: Not reported: the paper never says whether the test EMG is silent or voiced, which changes what the throat electrode's rank means.

M05.field: Subset selection in EMG/EEG/MEG/EMA/accel/magnetometer/video; EMG exhaustive 2,047-subset search exists
M05.note: The +35% relative 8->4 cost repeats EMG recognition (+32%, +36%) and exhaustive EMG subset search exists (2,047 subsets), so only its use with open-vocabulary synthesis WER is new.

M06.note: Same-lab standard encoder plus HiFi-GAN pipeline with only the first convolution resized.

M07.field: LM for text decoding; none for synthesis
M07.note: No use-time LM is normal for synthesis, though Whisper adds an implicit LM at evaluation.

M09.note: Not applicable to an offline synthesis study.

M10.note: Not applicable to an offline synthesis study.

M11.field: Text reference + ASR or human listeners
M11.note: Corpus text scored by ASR is standard; Whisper normalization is unstated.

M12.note: Behind: no seeds or variance, no held-out subset choice, and a ~35% baseline 8-10 points worse than the same lab's later reports, so the subset ranking sits inside seed noise.

M13.field: Record with reduced layout (11->8); device prototypes
M13.note: Not applicable as an offline study, but virtual deletion cannot support the device-design claims.

figures.caption: Verdicts compare the paper's choice for each component with common practice across 8,995 ledger entries on any sensor (silent speech, brain-to-text, lip reading), not only EMG papers.

figures.title: 8-electrode baseline vs. other reports of the same pipeline
figures.subtitle: Gaddy corpus, silent test, Whisper WER (%), lower is better
figures.caption: Same corpus, model family, vocoder and ASR. The paper's 8-electrode baseline sits about 8 points above three same-lab reports; a hollow marker is a value read from the paper's plot (about ±0.3).

figures.title: Cost of going from 8 to 4 electrodes
figures.subtitle: Different ASR and model generations: compare the relative change only
figures.caption: ASR and model generation differ between papers, so only the relative change is comparable. The 8-electrode value for this paper is read from its plot.

figures.title: Fine-tuning from 8 channels helps; channel dropout does not
figures.subtitle: Read from the paper's Fig. 3, run count not stated
figures.caption: Values read from the paper's Fig. 3 (about ±0.3). Pretraining on 8 electrodes lowers WER at 4–6 electrodes; dropout probability p > 0 beats p = 0 only at 5 electrodes.
